finding: The new H15 instruction says to report a provider-layer refusal as `needs-human: <says>` verbatim, but every provider-layer `says` ends with "; run /afk:setup; nothing was started". The setup summary then tells the human to run /afk:setup again, and "nothing was started" refers to a team run, not setup.
why: SKILL.md 'Done when' requires `needs-human` items to be 'named precisely'. A needs-human line that tells the human to rerun the command they are in sends them in a loop: a rerun hits the same provider-layer refusal (missing adapter function, no POSIX shell, timeout), because setup cannot fix it.
fix: Report only the cause in H15. Either name it as `needs-human: <says up to the first "; run /afk:setup">`, or have the check put the cause in its own field (for example `cause`) and report `needs-human: <cause>`.
evidence: MANIFEST.md:386-388 "A `provider-layer` refusal is not a missing entry: do not offer this row in the election, print no rule, wait for nothing, and report `needs-human: <says>`."; scripts/team/permission.py:59 "f\"{adapter['error']}; run {SETUP}; nothing was started\"" with SETUP = "/afk:setup" (permission.py:28)

finding: The delta adds a provider-layer branch that reports `needs-human`, while the row's Notes still say that with no human present the row is skipped and reports `skipped (user choice)`. The row does not say which status wins when there is no human present and the probe gives a provider-layer refusal.

criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros): missing negative case around a new guard
finding: The ownership guard on the main checkout's local file still has no test. Round 2 (tv-r2-001) named three untested guards; rounds 3 and 4 added tests for the home-directory guard and the `.git` name guard only. If the loop at lines 94-96 were deleted, the suite would stay green, and the check would count a main-checkout file that Claude Code skips. That gives a false ok.
why: PROVIDERS.md:181 and :187 state ownership as one of the conditions the adapter mirrors. Checked by reading all of scripts/tests/test_team_permission.py: no test uses chown, a symlink, os.geteuid or a non-owned path. Every fixture sits under pytest's tmp_path, which the test user owns, so `[ -O "$entry" ]` is always true. The r2 fix suggested a documented skip if a fixture was impractical. No such skip appears in the test file, DECISIONS.md or .claude/wiring-ious.md (searched for `owned`, `ownership`, `-O `).
fix: Off Windows and when the euid is not 0, add a case built on `_linked_worktree`. Make one guarded entry exist but belong to someone else, for example by replacing main/.claude with a symlink to a directory root owns (`-O` follows the link). Then call `_assert_main_file_unread(tree, home["env"])`. If no fixture can do this, record the gap as a named skip or an IOU so the hole is visible.
evidence: claude.sh:94-95 `for entry in "$top" "$main" "$top/.claude"; do` / `[ ! -e "$entry" ] || [ -O "$entry" ] || return 0`; the only main-checkout negative tests are test_team_permission.py:147 `test_a_linked_worktree_on_windows_skips_the_main_checkout_local_file`, :155 `test_a_main_checkout_at_the_home_directory_is_not_read`, :163 `test_a_git_dir_not_named_dot_git_is_not_read`; fixture test_team_permission.py:115 `main, tree = tmp_path / "main", tmp_path / "tree"`

finding: The comment above the main-checkout read in afk_claude_spawn_rule_files still gives the old set of conditions. It leaves out the git common directory named `.git` condition (f022), and it says 'outside the home directory' where the corrected rule (f001) is that the repository root is not the home directory. A repository under the home directory (for example ~/src/repo) is read.
why: f001 and f022 corrected the conditions in PROVIDERS.md (table row :181 and bullet :187), but this comment in the provider file restates them in its own words. An editor who trusts the comment could remove the `*/.git` guard at :90, or read 'outside the home directory' as a wider skip than :93 makes.
fix: Reword the comment to match the code and PROVIDERS.md, or point at PROVIDERS.md "Spawn allow rule". For example: '# The main checkout's local file counts only off Windows, when the git common dir is named .git, the root is not $HOME, and its entries are user-owned.'
evidence: claude.sh:87 `# The main checkout's local file counts only off Windows, outside the home directory, on user-owned entries.`; claude.sh:90 `case "$main" in */.git) top=${main%/.git} ;; *) return 0 ;; esac`; claude.sh:93 `[ "$(cd "$top" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" = "$home" ] && return 0`; corrected text PROVIDERS.md:181 `the git common directory is named .git, the main checkout's root is not $HOME`; PROVIDERS.md:187 `when the repository root is the home directory ... The adapter also skips the main checkout's file when the git common directory is not named .git`. Pattern used: read the whole provider file and grep the surface for `home directory` and `.git`.

finding: H15 now says that a `provider-layer` probe miss is not offered in the election and reports `needs-human: <says>` (fix for f024 and f021). The setup rules that setup reads first still say every miss on an opt-in row is classified `opt-in available` and joins the election, with accept running the fix. The MANIFEST opt-in tier paragraph and SKILL.md steps 2 and 3 have no exception for a row whose Probe names a different outcome.
why: f024's own evidence named MANIFEST.md:27-30 and SKILL.md step 3 as the reader that conflicts with the row. The fix changed only the row, so the general rule still reads the old way. An agent that classifies by SKILL.md step 2 ('opt-in available (tagged [opt-in] ...)') offers H15 in the election. On accept it runs the Fix (`rule --json`, which exits 1 on this path) and waits. That is the loop the correction removed.
fix: Add one clause to the MANIFEST 'Opt-in tier' paragraph, for example: 'unless the entry's Probe names another outcome for that miss (as H15 does for `provider-layer`)'. Add a matching pointer in SKILL.md step 2 or 3, or have step 3 defer to a row's own Probe outcome. MANIFEST.md is in 0009's Scope. SKILL.md is not, so editing it needs a recorded Scope extension like D-80 and D-82.
evidence: corrected MANIFEST.md:386-388 `A provider-layer refusal is not a missing entry: do not offer this row in the election, print no rule, wait for nothing, and report needs-human: <says>.`; stale MANIFEST.md:28-30 `a probe miss classifies opt-in available, never missing/broken. Offered at report time as an election on **every** branch, deselected by default; accept ⇒ run the fix`; stale skills/afk/setup/SKILL.md step 2 `opt-in available (tagged **[opt-in]**, a preference on offer — never a failure; tag semantics in the manifest header)` and step 3 `On **every** branch, entries probing opt-in available join the election too ... accepted ⇒ run the entry's fix in step 4`. Pattern used: grep of MANIFEST.md and SKILL.md for `election|opt-in available|needs-human`, then reading SKILL.md steps 1-6.

finding: D-75's reversal step says AFK_SPAWN_ALLOW_RULE lives in scripts/team/permission.py. It lives in hooks/lib/providers/claude.sh. Since f007's fix, it is a variable local to afk_claude_spawn_allow_rule, and the test's `_constant` regex pins it there. permission.py holds only INVOCATION.
